item.text: {"text":"Evidence supports testing text fusion, but does not establish that jointly trained, randomly initialized mean-pooled tokens improve HSTU. [TASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029) reports better accuracy and reduced popularity bias through text matching, but uses pretrained language models, so its gains do not directly transfer to this setting. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) warns that directly adding text and ID embeddings can be ineffective because their characteristics differ. [NISER](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04276) links popularity bias partly to embedding norms in session recommendation, motivating norm diagnostics without establishing the same mechanism in HSTU. The retrieved evidence does not directly demonstrate brand shortcuts or robustness to missing text for a from-scratch lexical encoder.\n\nUseful proposed ablations within one jointly trained HSTU: ID-only versus ID plus mean-pooled trainable text embeddings; title-only versus title plus description; fixed addition versus a learned residual gate; text dropout versus none. Use zero text contribution for empty fields and exclude padding from pooling. Test suspected shortcuts through title-derived brand-token masking and item-text shuffling within training-popularity bins; these are experimental controls, not established remedies. Keep splits, seeds, training budget and candidate evaluation fixed. Select by the prescribed macro validation HR@10; supplement with descriptive breakdowns by training-item frequency, text availability and title overlap, plus embedding-norm/popularity correlations. Improvements concentrated on frequent items or repeated brand tokens would warrant further investigation before attributing gains to finer product distinctions."}
